sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店当DJ的黑胶唱片时代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去上班，把DJ台变成一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, Steve Bannon walked out of the White House on Friday and headed straight back to Breitbart News.
sentences.zh: 今天，史蒂夫·班农周五走出了白宫，径直回到了布赖特巴特新闻网（Breitbart News）。

sentences.en: Will he use the alt-right megaphone to help the president who's just dismissed him or to hurt him?
sentences.zh: 他会利用这个另类右翼的扩音器去帮助那位刚刚解雇他的总统，还是去伤害他？

sentences.en: And will Steve Bannon at Breitbart be more powerful than Steve Bannon in the White House?
sentences.zh: 而且，在布赖特巴特新闻网的史蒂夫·班农会比在白宫的史蒂夫·班农更有权势吗？

sentences.en: It's Monday, August 21St.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月21日，星期一。

sentences.en: Jeremy Peters, where does the story of Breitbart and Steve Bannon begin?
sentences.zh: 杰里米·彼得斯，布赖特巴特新闻网和史蒂夫·班农的故事是从哪里开始的？

sentences.en: Michael, it starts when Andrew Breitbart, the founder of Breitbart News and its namesake, died in 2012.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，故事始于2012年，当时布赖特巴特新闻网的创始人兼同名者安德鲁·布赖特巴特去世了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Andrew Breitbart and Steve Bannon were partners in crime before Andrew's death.
sentences.zh: 安德鲁·布赖特巴特和史蒂夫·班农在安德鲁去世前就是“同谋”。

sentences.en: Steve served as kind of an informal editor, whisperer to Andrew before he took on any type of official capacity with Breitbart.
sentences.zh: 在史蒂夫担任布赖特巴特的任何正式职务之前，他更像是安德鲁的非正式编辑和幕后军师。

sentences.en: And what had Breitbart News been under Andrew Breitbart and what did it become under Steve Bannon?
sentences.zh: 那么在安德鲁·布赖特巴特领导下，布赖特巴特新闻网是什么样的？在史蒂夫·班农领导下又变成了什么样？

sentences.en: So Breitbart under Breitbart was more oriented toward gotcha videos.
sentences.zh: 在安德鲁领导下的布赖特巴特更倾向于制作那些“抓现行”的视频。

sentences.en: You'll remember that it was the place where a woman by the name of Shirley Sherrod, who was a Department of Agriculture employee,
sentences.zh: 你可能还记得，当时有一位名叫雪莉·谢罗德的女性，她是农业部的一名员工，

sentences.en: was filmed saying what appeared to be very disparaging things about white people and her refusal to help them when she was with the Department of Agriculture.
sentences.zh: 她被拍到说了一些似乎非常贬低白人的话，并声称她在农业部工作时拒绝帮助他们。

sentences.en: It turns out that that video had been selectively edited and left out some exculpatory information.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，那段视频经过了选择性剪辑，遗漏了一些能证明她清白的信息。

sentences.en: It made Sherrod look a lot worse than she really was and in fact twisted her words.
sentences.zh: 这让谢罗德看起来比实际情况糟糕得多，甚至扭曲了她的原话。

sentences.en: So after Andrew dies and Steve takes over, the site really begins to take up certain political causes that are rallying points for the Tea Party.
sentences.zh: 所以，在安德鲁去世、史蒂夫接手后，该网站真正开始承担起某些茶党（Tea Party）的集结号召任务。

sentences.en: And one of the big ones, of course, was the unseating of Eric Cantor.
sentences.zh: 当然，其中一件大事就是让埃里克·坎托下台。

sentences.en: To begin, though, with the major political upset for one of the most powerful Republicans in the country, Eric Cantor,
sentences.zh: 首先，让我们从全国最有权势的共和党人之一——埃里克·坎托遭遇的重大政治挫败说起，

sentences.en: the number two GOP lawmaker in the House, beaten in the primary by a Tea Party candidate.
sentences.zh: 作为众议院共和党二号人物，他在初选中被一名茶党候选人击败了。

sentences.en: And under Bannon, Breitbart really becomes more of a weapon for the Tea Party conservatives,
sentences.zh: 在班农的领导下，布赖特巴特真正成为了茶党保守派的武器，

sentences.en: the anti-establishment conservatives who want to unseat and defeat Republican Party leadership.
sentences.zh: 那些想要推翻和击败共和党领导层的反建制保守派。

sentences.en: Yep, that's right.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实如此。

sentences.en: Cantor lost to David Bratt, a political unknown.
sentences.zh: 坎托输给了政治素人戴夫·布拉特。

sentences.en: Cantor was widely thought to be the next Speaker of the House.
sentences.zh: 坎托曾被广泛认为是下一任众议院议长。

sentences.en: Breitbart, under Steve Bannon's direction, became one of the only media outlets paying any attention
sentences.zh: 在史蒂夫·班农的指导下，布赖特巴特成为唯一关注此事的媒体之一，

sentences.en: to this little-known economics professor named Dave Bratt, who was running in a primary challenge that everyone expected Bratt to lose.
sentences.zh: 关注着这位名不见经传的经济学教授戴夫·布拉特，他参加了一场所有人都认为他会输的初选挑战。

sentences.en: How much of an upset is this?
sentences.zh: 这算多大的冷门？

sentences.en: Cantor is the first person in American history to lose his primary while holding the position of House Majority Leader.
sentences.zh: 坎托是美国历史上第一位在担任众议院多数党领袖期间输掉初选的人。

sentences.en: They've gone from being on the bottom rung of the conservative media food chain to suddenly being capable of taking out the majority leader of the House of Representatives.
sentences.zh: 他们从保守派媒体食物链的最底层，突然变得有能力干掉众议院的多数党领袖。

sentences.en: So it becomes an enormously powerful weapon for the Tea Party right, especially as it begins to coalesce around opposing issues like immigration reform.
sentences.zh: 因此，它成为了茶党右翼极其强大的武器，尤其是在它开始围绕移民改革等反对议题凝聚力量时。

sentences.en: Breitbart had a huge role in publicizing what it saw as this shady, corrupt, backroom deal
sentences.zh: 布赖特巴特在曝光它所认为的这种阴暗、腐败的幕后交易中发挥了巨大作用，

sentences.en: that sell-out moderate Republicans were making with Democrats in the Senate in 2013 to pass an immigration bill.
sentences.zh: 即那些出卖原则的温和派共和党人在2013年与参议院民主党人达成的移民法案交易。

sentences.en: And this would have been, had it passed both houses Congress, the most significant immigration reform legislation in years and years.
sentences.zh: 如果该法案在国会两院通过，这将是多年来最重要的移民改革立法。

sentences.en: The sponsors that are producing legislation for us today will not say amazingly how many people they expect to enter into our country if their bill passes.
sentences.zh: 令人惊讶的是，今天为我们制定立法的发起人甚至说不出他们预计法案通过后会有多少人进入我国。

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: You don't know or you won't say.
sentences.zh: 你是不知道，还是不肯说？

sentences.en: But because of resistance from the right and from players like Breitbart, it never got off the ground.
sentences.zh: 但由于来自右翼和像布赖特巴特这样的参与者的阻挠，它从未启动。

sentences.en: This is legislation that is a flawed legislation, fatally flawed, and it should not become law.
sentences.zh: 这是一项有缺陷的立法，致命的缺陷，它不应该成为法律。

sentences.en: It just not.
sentences.zh: 就是不应该。

sentences.en: It shouldn't.
sentences.zh: 它不该通过。

sentences.en: And I think we've told this story before on The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我想我们之前在《每日新闻》里讲过这个故事。

sentences.en: Basically, Steve Bannon starts to work with then-Senator Jeff Sessions, who is an outspoken opponent of making it easier for illegal immigrants to stay in this country.
sentences.zh: 基本上，史蒂夫·班农开始与时任参议员杰夫·塞申斯合作，后者是放宽非法移民留美政策的直言不讳的反对者。

sentences.en: And Sessions 8 at the time, Stephen Miller, and like bells should be going off in people's heads here, to block this comprehensive immigration reform.
sentences.zh: 当时塞申斯的助手是斯蒂芬·米勒——人们听到这名字应该警觉起来——他们联手阻止了这项全面移民改革。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是这样。

sentences.en: And so, I mean, I remember the first time I ever met Stephen Miller was because Steve Bannon had suggested that I call him.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我记得我第一次见到斯蒂芬·米勒是因为史蒂夫·班农建议我给他打电话。

sentences.en: He said, hey, call up this guy who works for Jeff Sessions.
sentences.zh: 他说，嘿，给这个为杰夫·塞申斯工作的人打个电话。

sentences.en: He's really smart.
sentences.zh: 他非常聪明。

sentences.en: He knows immigration policy cold.
sentences.zh: 他对移民政策了如指掌。

sentences.en: He'll be a big asset to you.
sentences.zh: 他会是你的一大助力。

sentences.en: So even back in 2013-14, Bannon had forged a relationship with Jeff Sessions.
sentences.zh: 所以早在2013-2014年，班农就已经与杰夫·塞申斯建立了关系。

sentences.en: Bannon and Sessions and Steve Miller were in the thick of it together in this fight.
sentences.zh: 班农、塞申斯和斯蒂芬·米勒一起深陷在这场斗争中。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So all of this sets in motion, Steve Bannon, Jeff Sessions, and Stephen Miller coming together with Donald Trump, whose campaign at this point is, as I recall,
sentences.zh: 所以这一切促成了史蒂夫·班农、杰夫·塞申斯和斯蒂芬·米勒与唐纳德·特朗普的联手，据我回忆，当时特朗普的竞选活动，

sentences.en: kind of on the rocks.
sentences.zh: 有点摇摇欲坠。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And they all start to see Donald Trump as the candidate who can best embody these policies they have, right?
sentences.zh: 他们都开始把唐纳德·特朗普视为最能体现他们这些政策的候选人，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: Steve's affinity for Donald Trump was that Donald Trump was arguably the most anti-establishment politician you had running for the presidency in a generation.
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫对唐纳德·特朗普的青睐在于，唐纳德·特朗普可以说是这一代人中竞选总统的最反建制的政治家。

sentences.en: And they were laughing at me when I was saying, hey, this guy Trump is going to be, this is going to be very serious.
sentences.zh: 当我当时说“嘿，这个叫特朗普的家伙会很厉害，这会非常严肃”时，他们还在嘲笑我。

sentences.en: So it's good to see that you're in the heat of combat now.
sentences.zh: 所以很高兴看到你现在正处于战斗的热潮中。

sentences.en: Well, you know, I remember that well.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，我对此记忆犹新。

sentences.en: Trump would occasionally go on Bannon's Breitbart News radio show.
sentences.zh: 特朗普偶尔会去班农的布赖特巴特新闻广播节目。

sentences.en: Especially because I'd always mess up my hair when I put those big microphones around, you know, you'd always put them on.
sentences.zh: 特别是因为我总是把那些大麦克风放在周围时弄乱我的头发，你知道，你总是得戴上它们。

sentences.en: So I'd mess up my hair, which is fine.
sentences.zh: 所以我弄乱了头发，但这没关系。

sentences.en: But I remember that you looked and you said, boy, those are big crowds you're getting.
sentences.zh: 但我记得你看着我说，天哪，你吸引了这么多人群。

sentences.en: You have more than anybody else by far.
sentences.zh: 你的人数比任何人都多，多得多。

sentences.en: I said, Steve, I'm telling you, just watch.
sentences.zh: 我说，史蒂夫，我告诉你，看着吧。

sentences.en: And, you know, now we're getting, I mean, we had 20,000 in Dallas.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，现在我们的人数，我的意思是，我们在达拉斯有2万人。

sentences.en: Bannon always kind of had his eye on Trump as a figure people were underestimating politically.
sentences.zh: 班农一直把特朗普视为一个在政治上被人们低估的人物。

sentences.en: You know, we've had a lot of fun talking about very negative subjects because everything is negative with the country, Steve.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们聊了很多关于非常负面的话题，因为在这个国家，一切都是负面的，史蒂夫。

sentences.en: I mean, there's nothing good happening.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，没有任何好事发生。

sentences.en: There's nothing positive happening.
sentences.zh: 没有任何积极的事情发生。

sentences.en: We don't win anymore.
sentences.zh: 我们再也赢不了了。

sentences.en: So and if there's one reason that Bannon and Trump really hit it off,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果说班农和特朗普一拍即合有一个原因的话，

sentences.en: it was because they both shared this disgust for people who had been telling each of them all of their lives that they weren't going to be taken seriously.
sentences.zh: 那就是他们都对那些一生都在告诉他们“你不会被认真对待”的人怀有同样的厌恶。

sentences.en: And they both kind of harbored and nursed these these grudges that the elite institutions that they kind of operated at the at the periphery of or sometimes from inside Steve Bannon's case,
sentences.zh: 他们都怀揣并滋养着这些怨恨，针对那些他们处于边缘，或者有时像史蒂夫·班农那样从内部运作的精英机构，

sentences.en: Harvard, Goldman Sachs, Donald Trump's case, you know, New York Society, the Ivy League.
sentences.zh: 哈佛、高盛；对于唐纳德·特朗普来说，你知道，纽约上流社会、常春藤盟校。

sentences.en: They never really felt a part of it.
sentences.zh: 他们从未真正感到自己是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: They never really felt comfortable in their own skin within these rarefied worlds.
sentences.zh: 在这些高不可攀的世界里，他们从未真正感到自在。

sentences.en: And they both shared a disdain for the people who felt like those worlds were theirs and theirs alone.
sentences.zh: 他们都对那些认为这些世界只属于他们自己的人怀有蔑视。

sentences.en: Now, how did the destruction of the American financial system, the world financial system and the American political system take place?
sentences.zh: 那么，美国金融体系、世界金融体系和美国政治体系的破坏是如何发生的？

sentences.en: Tell me, how did that happen?
sentences.zh: 告诉我，那是怎么发生的？

sentences.en: When the biggest enemies we've had in the last hundred years, the Nazis, the communists, the fascists, imperial Japan, even Osama bin Laden,
sentences.zh: 当我们过去一百年里最大的敌人——纳粹、共产主义者、法西斯、日本帝国，甚至奥萨马·本·拉登，

sentences.en: not one of our enemies could ever destroy our financial and political system.
sentences.zh: 没有一个敌人能摧毁我们的金融和政治体系。

sentences.en: They couldn't even imagine it.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至无法想象。

sentences.en: How did it happen?
sentences.zh: 那是怎么发生的？

sentences.en: Quite easily.
sentences.zh: 非常容易。

sentences.en: In the last 20 years, our financial elites and the political class have taken care of themselves and led our country to the brink of ruin.
sentences.zh: 在过去的20年里，我们的金融精英和政治阶层只顾自己，把我们的国家推向了毁灭的边缘。

sentences.en: I guess it's important to note here that another thing that binds these two men, Steve Bannon and Donald Trump, is that they view the Republican Party with immense suspicion.
sentences.zh: 我想这里需要指出的是，将史蒂夫·班农和唐纳德·特朗普这两个人联系在一起的另一件事是，他们对共和党怀有极大的怀疑。

sentences.en: And yet they're using the Republican Party as a vehicle to try to get Donald Trump elected.
sentences.zh: 然而，他们正在利用共和党作为工具，试图让唐纳德·特朗普当选。

sentences.en: It's really kind of a complicated thing happening.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一件复杂的事情。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it becomes ultimately, I think, more than just a vehicle to get Donald Trump elected.
sentences.zh: 我认为，最终这不仅仅是让唐纳德·特朗普当选的工具。

sentences.en: It becomes a vehicle to dismantle the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 它成为了拆解共和党的工具。

sentences.en: Only operating from within inside it are you able to really defeat it.
sentences.zh: 只有从内部运作，你才能真正击败它。

sentences.en: I think the big surprise is whether we're watching a switcheroo, one of the biggest ever in politics.
sentences.zh: 我认为最大的惊喜在于我们是否正在目睹一场政治史上最大的“偷梁换柱”。

sentences.en: So almost exactly a year ago today, you have the situation where Paul Manafort, the former Trump campaign manager,
sentences.zh: 就在大约一年前的今天，出现了这样一种情况：前特朗普竞选经理保罗·马纳福特，

sentences.en: is found after a New York Times report to have concealed this income from Ukrainian sources.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》报道后被发现隐瞒了来自乌克兰的收入。

sentences.en: That's hugely problematic for him.
sentences.zh: 这对他是极其严重的麻烦。

sentences.en: Trump reads this in the New York Times, gets furious and ends up shaking up his whole campaign team.
sentences.zh: 特朗普在《纽约时报》上读到这个消息，勃然大怒，最终改组了他的整个竞选团队。

sentences.en: He's been basically forced out by two people coming in now who come in from the so-called dark side of politics who are expected to make Trump even more abrasive and more pugilistic.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是被现在进来的两个人赶走的，他们来自所谓的政治“黑暗面”，预计会让特朗普变得更加尖锐和好斗。

sentences.en: Bringing in Steve Bannon and Kellyanne Conway to run the show.
sentences.zh: 引入史蒂夫·班农和凯莉安·康威来掌管大局。

sentences.en: And they are largely credited with helping the Trump campaign develop a level of focus in the final two and a half months that allowed Trump to win.
sentences.zh: 他们被广泛认为帮助特朗普竞选团队在最后两个半月里达到了某种专注度，从而使特朗普获胜。

sentences.en: More than just keeping Trump focused and as on message as you can keep Donald Trump, Steve brought a level of ruthlessness to the campaign's attacks on Hillary Clinton,
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是让特朗普保持专注并尽可能传达信息，史蒂夫还为竞选团队对希拉里·克林顿的攻击带来了一种无情，

sentences.en: which were already pretty savage.
sentences.zh: 而这些攻击本身已经相当凶狠了。

sentences.en: Donald Trump just dropped a new element into the pre-debate atmosphere with a little more than an hour to go before tonight's event.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普在今晚的活动开始前一个多小时，向辩论前的氛围中投下了一个新元素。

sentences.en: It was Steve Bannon whose idea was to bring out the accusers of Bill Clinton's.
sentences.zh: 正是史蒂夫·班农提议带出比尔·克林顿的指控者。

sentences.en: From left to right, Kathleen Willey, Juanita Broderick, then Donald Trump in the middle, Paula Jones.
sentences.zh: 从左到右，凯瑟琳·威利、胡安妮塔·布罗德里克，中间是唐纳德·特朗普，还有宝拉·琼斯。

sentences.en: Bannon brings them to a presidential debate and wants to seat them in Trump's guest box where they will be right next to Bill and Chelsea Clinton.
sentences.zh: 班农把她们带到了总统辩论现场，并想让她们坐在特朗普的嘉宾席上，紧挨着比尔和切尔西·克林顿。

sentences.en: The key point that Donald Trump has been trying to make on Twitter and has been trying to use Breitbart News, which is a conservative news outlet,
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普一直试图在推特上表达的关键点，以及他一直试图利用布赖特巴特新闻网——一家保守派新闻媒体——所做的，

sentences.en: the head of which or former head of which is effectively running Trump's campaign.
sentences.zh: 其负责人或前负责人实际上正在经营特朗普的竞选活动。

sentences.en: They've been all day long pushing out the notion that.
sentences.zh: 他们整天都在推销这个概念。

sentences.en: And they hold a press conference before the debate.
sentences.zh: 他们在辩论前举行了新闻发布会。

sentences.en: And in the back of that room where the press conference is being held, there are pictures of Steve Bannon smiling, this ear-to-ear grin.
sentences.zh: 在举行新闻发布会的房间后面，有史蒂夫·班农微笑着的照片，露出了咧到耳根的笑容。

sentences.en: He is just absolutely thrilled at what he's pulled off.
sentences.zh: 他对自己的所作所为感到无比兴奋。

sentences.en: Mr. Trump may have said some bad words, but Bill Clinton raped me and Hillary Clinton threatened me.
sentences.zh: 特朗普先生可能说过一些坏话，但比尔·克林顿强奸了我，希拉里·克林顿威胁了我。

sentences.en: I don't think there's any comparison.
sentences.zh: 我认为两者没有可比性。

sentences.en: So, Jeremy, let's fast forward to the White House.
sentences.zh: 那么，杰里米，让我们快进到白宫时期。

sentences.en: Donald Trump is elected with Steve Bannon as a top advisor and guide throughout the campaign.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普当选，史蒂夫·班农在整个竞选过程中担任高级顾问和向导。

sentences.en: And you have Bannon, Sessions, and Miller all constituting a nationalist faction inside the administration.
sentences.zh: 班农、塞申斯和米勒构成了政府内部的民族主义派系。

sentences.en: And in some ways, this group of nationalists is extremely effective when they get to the White House in setting an agenda.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，这群民族主义者在进入白宫制定议程时非常有效。

sentences.en: And in others, they almost derail the first year of the presidency, right?
sentences.zh: 而在另一些方面，他们几乎让总统任期的第一年脱轨了，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，正是这样。

sentences.en: I mean, they are responsible, of course, for one of the biggest and earliest missteps of the Trump presidency, which is its first travel ban,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们当然要为特朗普总统任期内最早、最大的失误之一负责，那就是第一次旅行禁令，

sentences.en: which blocked people from mostly Muslim countries from entering the United States.
sentences.zh: 该禁令阻止了来自大多数穆斯林国家的人进入美国。

sentences.en: Steve Bannon and Stephen Miller were responsible for seeing this through.
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫·班农和斯蒂芬·米勒负责推动了这一政策。

sentences.en: And it kept getting kicked down by the courts.
sentences.zh: 但它不断被法院驳回。

sentences.en: What they would say they are proud of achieving, I think, most of all, is the withdrawal from the Paris Climate Accords,
sentences.zh: 我认为他们最引以为傲的成就，是退出《巴黎气候协定》，

sentences.en: which perfectly fits with Steve Bannon's worldview that the United States should not be beholden to the interests of other nations.
sentences.zh: 这完全符合史蒂夫·班农的世界观，即美国不应受制于其他国家的利益。

sentences.en: The Paris Agreement handicaps the United States economy in order to win praise from the very foreign capitals and global activists that have long sought to gain wealth at our country's expense.
sentences.zh: 《巴黎协定》阻碍了美国经济的发展，以换取那些长期寻求以牺牲我国利益为代价获取财富的外国首都和全球活动家的赞扬。

sentences.en: So, Jeremy, I want to come back to where we started, where, in a sense, Bannon started and where he returns, which is to Breitbart News.
sentences.zh: 所以，杰里米，我想回到我们开始的地方，从某种意义上说，班农开始的地方，也是他回归的地方，那就是布赖特巴特新闻网。

sentences.en: So, let's just dissect a few of the things that have happened in the past couple of days.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们剖析一下过去几天发生的一些事情。

sentences.en: First, an editor at Breitbart, shortly after the news is announced, tweets the word war.
sentences.zh: 首先，在消息宣布后不久，布赖特巴特的一位编辑在推特上发了一个词：“战争”。

sentences.en: And then Bannon goes back to Breitbart, presides over a meeting, and offers this very intriguing quote that the Trump presidency that we fought for and won is over.
sentences.zh: 然后班农回到布赖特巴特，主持了一次会议，并引用了一句非常耐人寻味的话：“我们为之奋斗并赢得的特朗普总统任期已经结束了。”

sentences.en: What does that mean?
sentences.zh: 那是什么意思？

sentences.en: I mean, Breitbart was always kind of weaponized media.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，布赖特巴特一直是一种武器化的媒体。

sentences.en: As far as pro-Trump conservatives were concerned, it was their tool, you know, kind of their hammer with which to bludgeon the Republican establishment.
sentences.zh: 就支持特朗普的保守派而言，它是他们的工具，你知道，就像他们用来打击共和党建制派的锤子。

sentences.en: I think now it becomes this heat-seeking missile directed straight at Paul Ryan and Mitch McConnell.
sentences.zh: 我认为现在它变成了一枚直接瞄准保罗·瑞安和米奇·麦康奈尔的寻热导弹。

sentences.en: I think what Steve sees happening in his ideal world is a party that emerges from Donald Trump's presidency that is neither Republican nor Democrat.
sentences.zh: 我认为史蒂夫在他理想的世界中看到的是，一个从唐纳德·特朗普总统任期中崛起的政党，既不是共和党也不是民主党。

sentences.en: I think if you were to ask him, and I've heard him say this before, he thinks that the Republican Party is basically done as an institution.
sentences.zh: 我想如果你问他——我以前听他这么说过——他认为共和党作为一个机构基本上已经完了。

sentences.en: The establishment, and particularly the Republican establishment, has no interest in making the fundamental changes in this country that we have to do in order to save our country.
sentences.zh: 建制派，特别是共和党建制派，根本没有兴趣做出我们为了拯救国家而必须做出的根本性改变。

sentences.en: He's somebody who has these grand theories of societal, cultural destruction and rebirth.
sentences.zh: 他是一个拥有社会、文化破坏与重生宏大理论的人。

sentences.en: What we need to do is bitch-slap the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 我们需要做的是给共和党一记耳光。

sentences.en: And he sees the Republican Party as, if not American society or the world at large, in the throes of a great crisis from which it will have to reinvent itself.
sentences.zh: 他认为共和党——如果不是美国社会或整个世界的话——正处于一场巨大的危机之中，必须从中自我重塑。

sentences.en: And if we have to, we'll take it over.
sentences.zh: 如果必须的话，我们会接管它。

sentences.en: Is Breitbart poised to be even stronger than ever now with a leader who helped elect the president and enact a nationalist agenda in the White House?
sentences.zh: 布赖特巴特新闻网现在是否准备好变得比以往任何时候都更强大？毕竟它的领导者曾帮助总统当选，并在白宫推行了民族主义议程。

sentences.en: Is Bannon better equipped now to reshape the Republican Party?
sentences.zh: 班农现在是否更有能力重塑共和党？

sentences.en: When we started this conversation, you said that that was an overriding goal of his, to turn this party inside out, maybe even blow it up.
sentences.zh: 在我们开始这段对话时，你说过这是他的首要目标，即彻底改变这个党，甚至可能将其摧毁。

sentences.en: Is he more able to do that on the outside of Breitbart than he was inside the White House?
sentences.zh: 相比在白宫内部，他在布赖特巴特新闻网外部是否更有能力做到这一点？

sentences.en: I think, to a certain extent, yes.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，我认为是的。

sentences.en: He will be unshackled in a way that, for instance, frees him from having to pretend like he cares about working with Mitch McConnell and Paul Ryan, which,
sentences.zh: 他将以一种前所未有的方式获得自由，例如，他不必再假装关心与米奇·麦康奈尔和保罗·瑞安的合作，而这，

sentences.en: as the president's chief strategist, he had to do inside the White House.
sentences.zh: 作为总统的首席战略顾问，他在白宫内部是必须做的。

sentences.en: Now he's able to attack them and question their conservative credentials and their commitment to Trump's agenda and energize and mobilize a very rowdy and passionate part of the conservative base.
sentences.zh: 现在他可以攻击他们，质疑他们的保守派资历以及他们对特朗普议程的承诺，并激励和动员保守派基础中非常吵闹和充满激情的一部分人。

sentences.en: The ultimate success for Steve Bannon having now left the White House will be if he is able to completely obliterate the leadership structure of the Republican Party and replace it with something that more closely aligns with his conservative,
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫·班农离开白宫后的最终成功，将取决于他是否能够彻底摧毁共和党的领导结构，并用一种更符合他保守的、

sentences.en: nationalistic, America-first view of policy.
sentences.zh: 民族主义的、“美国优先”政策观的东西取而代之。

sentences.en: And where all the energy is right now is the Trump wing of the party.
sentences.zh: 而目前所有的能量都集中在共和党的特朗普派系上。

sentences.en: And I think that if Steve Bannon comes out of 2018 with a Republican Party in tatters,
sentences.zh: 我认为，如果史蒂夫·班农在2018年之后让共和党变得支离破碎，

sentences.en: he'll consider that to be a victory because it'll just be one step closer to what he sees as his goal of entirely remaking it into a party devoted more to economic nationalism.
sentences.zh: 他会认为这是一场胜利，因为这将使他离自己的目标更近一步，即将其完全改造成一个更致力于经济民族主义的政党。

sentences.en: The party of Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普的政党。

sentences.en: Maybe even a new party.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能是一个新政党。

sentences.en: Maybe call it the Trump independence party.
sentences.zh: 也许可以叫它特朗普独立党。

sentences.en: But I think that's where Steve sees his head of Donald Trump as the catalyst for shattering the Republican Party as we know it and becoming kind of a figurehead around which a new party develops.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这就是史蒂夫眼中的愿景，他将唐纳德·特朗普视为粉碎我们所知的共和党的催化剂，并成为一个新政党围绕其发展的某种象征性人物。

sentences.en: We assembled here today are issuing a new decree to be heard in every city, in every foreign capital and in every hall of power.
sentences.zh: 今天聚集在这里的我们，正在发布一项新的法令，要让每一座城市、每一个外国首都和每一个权力大厅都能听到。

sentences.en: From this day forward, a new vision will govern our land.
sentences.zh: 从今天起，一个新的愿景将治理我们的国家。

sentences.en: From this day forward, it's going to be only America firSt.
sentences.zh: 从今天起，只有美国优先。

sentences.en: America firSt.
sentences.zh: 美国优先。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼等等。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无保留、未经修饰的对话实况。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在NYTimes.com上直播精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的事情。

sentences.en: What we know is that resistance is not something you say, it's something you do.
sentences.zh: 我们所知道的是，抵抗不是说出来的，而是做出来的。

sentences.en: Tens of thousands of protesters across the country came out this weekend to demonstrate against racism, white supremacy, and Nazism, one week after the violence in Charlottesville.
sentences.zh: 在夏洛茨维尔暴力事件发生一周后，全国各地成千上万的抗议者在这个周末走上街头，反对种族主义、白人至上主义和纳粹主义。

sentences.en: We're going to stand up for each other because we know what it's like to walk alone.
sentences.zh: 我们要互相支持，因为我们知道独自前行是什么滋味。

sentences.en: If you're black, if you're brown, if you're queer, if you're a woman.
sentences.zh: 无论你是黑人、棕色人种、酷儿，还是女性。

sentences.en: On Saturday, President Trump tweeted that he wanted to applaud the protesters in Boston, the site of the biggest demonstration, saying they were, quote,
sentences.zh: 周六，特朗普总统发推文称，他想为波士顿的抗议者鼓掌，那是规模最大的示威地点，他说他们是在，引用的话，

sentences.en: speaking out against bigotry and hate.
sentences.zh: 大声反对偏执和仇恨。

sentences.en: Our country will soon come together as one, he said.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们的国家很快就会团结一致。

sentences.en: Our great country has been divided for decades.
sentences.zh: 我们伟大的国家几十年来一直处于分裂状态。

sentences.en: Sometimes you need protest in order to heal.
sentences.zh: 有时你需要抗议才能实现治愈。

sentences.en: And we will heal and be stronger than ever before.
sentences.zh: 我们将治愈并变得比以往任何时候都更强大。

sentences.en: And the first total coast-to-coast solar eclipse in nearly a century occurs today.
sentences.zh: 今天将出现近一个世纪以来的首次横跨全美的日全食。

sentences.en: It will begin in Oregon around 10.15 a.m.
sentences.zh: 它将于上午10点15分左右在俄勒冈州开始。

sentences.en: West Coast time and end in South Carolina around 2.49 p.m.
sentences.zh: 西海岸时间，并于下午2点49分左右在南卡罗来纳州结束。

sentences.en: East Coast time.
sentences.zh: 东海岸时间。

sentences.en: Along the course of the eclipse, known as the Path of Totality, the sun will appear to be completely blotted out by the moon, with only a thin corona of light visible.
sentences.zh: 在日食的路径上，即所谓的全食带，太阳看起来将被月亮完全遮住，只剩下一圈薄薄的光环可见。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 选举迎来了一群自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场激烈、混乱，有时甚至令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《Metro》中，我和莎拉·凯尼格将讲述人们试图维持影响力，却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《Metro》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 在任何你收听播客的地方都可以收听。
